translation: I like open-world games.
wm: an open-world game
A big game world you can explore freely.
wb: オープンワールド：from English "open world"
sm: They enjoy games with big free worlds.
sb: ゲームが好き。：I like games
se: I like open-world games.
I'm into open-world games.
Open-world games are my favourite.

sentence: 技術の進歩はすごいね。
video_line: …のオカリナは技術の進歩だけでは放射できない何か…
video_front: 技術の進歩だけでは…
video_en: Technical progress alone...
translation: Technological progress is amazing.
wm: progress, advance
技術の進歩 = technological progress.
se: Technological progress is amazing.
Tech has come so far.
The progress in technology is incredible.

sentence: 車を盗まれた。
video_line: …自由にあったことだ車を盗んだり法律を破ったり…
translation: My car got stolen.
note: 盗まれた = was stolen.
wm: to steal
盗まれる = to have something stolen.
se: My car got stolen.
Someone stole my car.
I had my car stolen.

sentence: それは法律で決まってる。
video_line: …あったことだ車を盗んだり法律を破ったり通行人を襲…
video_front: 車を盗んだり、法律を破ったり。
video_en: Stealing cars, breaking the law.
translation: That's set by law.
wm: the law, a law
法律を破る = to break the law.
sm: A rule is fixed by law.
sb: 法律で決まってる。：is decided by law
se: That's set by law.
That's the law.
It's fixed by law.

sentence: 通行人に道を聞いた。
video_line: …んだり法律を破ったり通行人を襲ったり現実なら…
video_front: 通行人を襲ったり。
video_en: Attacking passers-by.
translation: I asked a passer-by for directions.
wm: a passer-by, a pedestrian
In open-world games, the NPCs walking around.
sm: They asked someone on the street for the way.
sb: Whole: I asked a passer-by for directions.
se: I asked a passer-by for directions.
I asked someone walking past for directions.
I asked a stranger the way.

sentence: 暴力はよくない。
video_line: …友達がゲームの中の暴力はあんなに楽しんでるのを見て…
video_front: ゲームの中の暴力はあんなに楽しんでるのを見て…
video_en: Seeing them enjoy the violence in the game that much...
translation: Violence is wrong.
wm: violence
暴力的 = violent.
se: Violence is wrong.
Violence is bad.
You shouldn't use violence.

sentence: この部屋は居心地がいい。
video_line: …んなに楽しんでるのを見て少し居心地の悪さを感じることもあった…
video_front: 少し居心地の悪さを感じることもあった。
video_en: Sometimes I felt a bit uncomfortable.
translation: This room is comfortable to be in.
note: 居心地が悪い = uncomfortable.
wm: how comfortable it feels to be somewhere
居心地がいい = cosy, comfortable; 居心地が悪い = awkward, uncomfortable.
wb: Whole: how your heart feels in a place.
sm: The room feels nice to be in.
sb: Whole: this room is comfortable to be in.
se: This room is comfortable to be in.
This room is so cosy.
I feel at home in this room.

sentence: ゲームを起動した。
video_line: …家に帰るとゲームキューブを起動して風のタクトのオ…
video_cut: ゲームキューブを起動
video_front: ゲームキューブを起動して…
video_en: I'd switch on the GameCube...
translation: I started up the game.
wm: starting up, booting (a machine or app)
起動する = to launch, to boot up.
sb: Whole: I started up the game.
se: I started up the game.
I booted up the game.
I launched the game.

sentence: 船で大海原に出た。
video_line: …起動して風のタクトの大海原への船を出してた水平線…
video_front: 風のタクトの大海原へ船を出してた。
video_en: And set sail across the great ocean of The Wind Waker.
translation: We set out onto the open ocean by boat.
wm: the great open ocean
Poetic word for a wide sea. 風のタクト is set on one.
sm: They sailed out into the wide sea.
sb: 大海原に出た。：went out onto the open ocean
Whole: we set out onto the open ocean by boat.
se: We set out onto the open ocean by boat.
We sailed out onto the open sea.
We took the boat out into the great ocean.

sentence: 水平線の向こうに島が見える。
video_line: …大海原への船を出してた水平線の向こうに何が待ってる…
video_front: 水平線の向こうに何が待ってるのか。
video_en: What was waiting beyond the horizon.
translation: I can see an island beyond the horizon.
wm: the horizon (where sea meets sky)
On land it's 地平線.
wb: Whole: the flat line of water.
sm: An island appears in the distance.
sb: 水平線の向こうに：beyond the horizon
島が見える。：an island can be seen
Whole: I can see an island beyond the horizon.
se: I can see an island beyond the horizon.
There's an island past the horizon.
Out on the horizon, I can see an island.

sentence: 新しいゲーム、ワクワクする！
video_line: …発見することが僕にとってのワクワクだったんだまあもちろんね…
video_front: それを発見することが、僕にとってのワクワクだったんだ。
video_en: Discovering that was what excited me.
translation: A new game, I'm so excited!
wm: excited, thrilled (about something coming)
ワクワクする = to be excited.
wb: ワクワク：sound word for excitement
sm: They're excited about a new game.
sb: 新しいゲーム、：a new game
Whole: a new game, I'm so excited!
se: A new game, I'm so excited!
I can't wait to play the new game!
New game, so exciting!

sentence: 子供の頃、このゲームに夢中だった。
video_line: …に惹かれていたゼルダで僕が夢中になったのは好き勝手に…
translation: As a kid, I was hooked on this game.
wm: absorbed, crazy about, hooked
〜に夢中 = hooked on ...
sm: They were obsessed with this game as a kid.
sb: このゲームに夢中だった。：was hooked on this game
Whole: as a kid, I was hooked on this game.
se: As a kid, I was hooked on this game.
I was obsessed with this game as a kid.
This game was my everything when I was young.

sentence: 好き勝手にやっていいよ。
video_line: …ルダで僕が夢中になったのは好き勝手に何でもできる自由じゃない誰…
video_front: ゼルダで僕が夢中になったのは、好き勝手に何でもできる自由じゃない。
video_en: What hooked me on Zelda wasn't the freedom to do whatever I wanted.
translation: Do whatever you like.
wm: doing whatever you please
Can be neutral (freedom) or critical (selfish).
sb: やっていいよ。：you can do
se: Do whatever you like.
Do as you please.
Feel free to do whatever.

sentence: みんなで一つの作品を作り上げた。
video_line: …自由じゃない誰かが想像して作り上げた世界を自分の足で…
video_front: 誰かが想像して作り上げた世界を…
video_en: A world someone imagined and built...
translation: We all built one piece of work together.
wm: to build up, to complete, to create (with effort)
Stresses finishing something built over time.
sb: 一つの作品を：one piece of work
Whole: we all built one piece of work together.
se: We all built one piece of work together.
We created one work as a team.
Together, we put one piece together.

sentence: 目標を達成した！
video_line: …残ることは全く別の達成なんだここにはゲーム作…
video_front: 全く別の達成なんだ。
video_en: It's a completely different achievement.
translation: I achieved my goal!
wm: achievement, accomplishment
達成する = to achieve. 目標を達成 = reach a goal.
sm: They reached what they aimed for.
se: I achieved my goal!
I reached my goal!
Goal accomplished!

sentence: このゲームは本当に優れている。
video_line: …大切なことを教えてくれる優れたゲームかどうかは与えられる…
video_front: 優れたゲームかどうかは…
video_en: Whether a game is great or not...
translation: This game is truly excellent.
wm: to excel, to be superior
Often 優れた (excellent) or 優れている.
sm: The game is of very high quality.
sb: Whole: this game is truly excellent.
se: This game is truly excellent.
This game is outstanding.
It's a genuinely great game.

sentence: 好奇心が強いね。
video_line: …決まらない僕たちの注意とか好奇心をどれだけたくみに導ける…
translation: You're very curious, huh.
wm: curiosity
好奇心が強い = very curious.
wb: Whole: a heart that likes the unusual.
sm: Someone always wants to know more.
se: You're very curious, huh.
You're so curious.
You've got a lot of curiosity.

sentence: 彼は言葉を巧みに使う。
video_line: …好奇心をどれだけたくみに導けるかにもかかっている…
translation: He uses words skilfully.
note: 巧みに = skilfully.
wm: skilful, clever, deft
巧みに = skilfully. Formal-ish.
se: He uses words skilfully.
He's very good with words.
He has a way with words.

sentence: 音が僕たちを導いてくれる。
video_line: …奇心をどれだけたくみに導けるかにもかかっているそこ…
video_front: 僕たちの注意とか好奇心を、どれだけ巧みに導けるかにもかかっている。
video_en: It also depends on how skilfully it can guide our attention and curiosity.
translation: The sound guides us.
wm: to guide, to lead
Lead someone along a path or to a result.
sm: The game's sound shows the way.
se: The sound guides us.
The sound leads the way.
The audio guides us along.

sentence: 可能性は無限にある。
video_line: …の天才性があると思う無限にできることを与える必要なん…
video_front: 無限にできることを与える必要なんてなかった。
video_en: There was no need to give us endless things to do.
translation: The possibilities are infinite.
wm: infinity, endless
無限に = endlessly.
sm: There's no end to what's possible.
se: The possibilities are infinite.
The possibilities are endless.
There's no limit to what's possible.

sentence: 日本のクリエイターは本当にすごい。
video_line: …30年近く前日本のクリエイターたちは小さなプラスチックの…
video_cut: 30年近く前日本のクリエイター
video_front: 30年近く前、日本のクリエイターたちは…
video_en: Nearly 30 years ago, Japanese creators...
translation: Japanese creators are truly amazing.
wm: a creator (of games, videos, art)
YouTubers are often called クリエイター too.
sm: People who make things in Japan are impressive.
sb: 日本のクリエイターは：Japanese creators
本当にすごい。：are really amazing
Whole: Japanese creators are truly amazing.
se: Japanese creators are truly amazing.
Japan's creators are incredible.
Japanese creators really are something.

sentence: やがて雨がやんだ。
video_line: …代や記憶の一部になりやがて日本という国を理解するき…
translation: Eventually the rain stopped.
wm: eventually, before long
A little literary; common in narration.
wb: やがて：adverb for before long (軈て)
sm: After a while, it stopped raining.
se: Eventually the rain stopped.
Before long, the rain stopped.
The rain eventually let up.

sentence: このゲームが日本語を始めたきっかけです。
video_line: …がて日本という国を理解するきっかけにもなったそしてアメリカ…
video_front: やがて日本という国を理解するきっかけにもなった。
video_en: Eventually it even became my way into understanding Japan.
meaning: trigger, the thing that started it
translation: This game is what got me started on Japanese.
wm: a trigger, a chance, the thing that started something
〜のきっかけ = what got you into ...
wb: きっかけ：word for trigger (切っ掛け)
sm: A game is why they began learning Japanese.
sb: きっかけです。：is the trigger
Whole: this game is what got me started on Japanese.
se: This game is what got me started on Japanese.
This game got me into Japanese.
I started Japanese because of this game.

sentence: これは本当に傑作だ。
video_line: …かもしれないけどゲームを傑作にするのに派手な演出を…
video_front: ゲームを傑作にするのに…
video_en: To make a game a masterpiece...
translation: This is truly a masterpiece.
wm: a masterpiece
The best work of an artist or studio.
sm: They think the game is a top work.
sb: 本当に傑作だ。：is truly a masterpiece
Whole: this is truly a masterpiece.
se: This is truly a masterpiece.
This really is a masterpiece.
A genuine masterpiece.

sentence: 最後の演出がすごかった。
video_line: …ームを傑作にするのに派手な演出を何もかも詰め込む必要…
translation: The final staging was amazing.
wm: presentation, staging, how a scene is directed
In games: cutscenes, effects, music cues.
sb: 最後の演出が：the final staging
Whole: the final staging was amazing.
se: The final staging was amazing.
The ending was beautifully done.
That final sequence was incredible.

sentence: 一つのゲームに全部詰め込んだ。
video_line: …派手な演出を何もかも詰め込む必要はないんだと思う必要な…
video_front: 派手な演出を何もかも詰め込む必要はないんだと思う。
video_en: I don't think you need to cram in every flashy effect.
translation: They crammed everything into one game.
wm: to cram, to pack in
Packing in as much as possible.
sm: One game has everything in it.
sb: 一つのゲームに：into one game
Whole: they crammed everything into one game.
se: They crammed everything into one game.
Everything got packed into one game.
They stuffed it all into a single game.

sentence: ゲームも芸術だと思う。
video_line: …なのは人の心に残る芸術を作ろうとすることそして何…
video_front: 人の心に残る芸術を作ろうとすること。
video_en: Trying to make art that stays in people's hearts.
translation: I think games are art too.
wm: art, the arts
芸術的 = artistic.
sm: They believe games count as art.
sb: 芸術だと思う。：are art, I think
Whole: I think games are art too.
se: I think games are art too.
Games are an art form too.
I'd say games are art as well.

sentence: このゲームには作った人の愛情を感じる。
video_line: …ことそして何より大きな愛情なんじゃないかなそこで冒…
video_front: 何より、大きな愛情なんじゃないかな。
video_en: And above all, a lot of love, I think.
translation: I can feel the creators' love in this game.
wm: love, affection, care
Love and care put into something, or for people.
sm: The makers clearly cared about the game.
sb: このゲームには：in this game
作った人の愛情を：the creators' love
Whole: I can feel the creators' love in this game.
se: I can feel the creators' love in this game.
You can feel how much the makers loved this game.
This game was made with love.

sentence: 動画の冒頭でも言ったけど。
video_line: …愛情なんじゃないかなそこで冒頭の問いに戻りたい実在しな…
translation: Like I said at the start of the video.
wm: the beginning, the opening (of a video, talk, book)
冒頭で = at the start.
sm: They refer back to what they said at the start.
sb: 動画の冒頭でも：at the start of the video too
Whole: like I said at the start of the video.
se: Like I said at the start of the video.
As I mentioned at the beginning.
I said this at the start of the video too.

sentence: その問いに答えるのは難しい。
video_line: …じゃないかなそこで冒頭の問いに戻りたい実在しなかったはずの…
video_front: そこで冒頭の問いに戻りたい。
video_en: So I want to go back to the question from the start.
translation: That question is hard to answer.
wm: a question
A bit more formal than 質問; common in writing and narration.
sm: The question doesn't have an easy answer.
sb: Whole: that question is hard to answer.
se: That question is hard to answer.
That's a tough question to answer.
It's hard to answer that question.

sentence: 物理的に無理だよ。
translation: It's physically impossible.
wm: physical, physically
物理的に無理 = physically impossible.
wb: Whole: by the logic of things.
se: It's physically impossible.
That's physically impossible.
There's no way, physically.

sentence: チャンネル登録してくれてありがとう！
video_line: …動画が面白いって思ったらチャンネル登録宜しくお願いします時のオカリナ…
video_front: チャンネル登録よろしくお願いします。
video_en: Please subscribe to the channel.
translation: Thanks for subscribing!
wm: subscribing to a YouTube channel
YouTubers end with チャンネル登録よろしくお願いします.
sm: A YouTuber thanks viewers for subscribing.
sb: くれてありがとう！：thanks for doing for me
se: Thanks for subscribing!
Thank you for subscribing!
Thanks for the sub!
